# Zydis provenance

## Source

- Repository: `https://github.com/zyantific/zydis.git`, vendored as the git
  submodule `zydis.submodule`.
- Pinned tag: `v4.1.1`
- Pinned commit: `a2278f1d254e492f6a6b39f6cb5d1f5d515659dc`
- Nested submodule (Zydis's own dependency): `dependencies/zycore` ->
  `https://github.com/zyantific/zycore-c`, commit
  `0b2432ced0884fd152b471d97ecf0258ff4d859f`.
- License: MIT (`LICENSE` in this folder, copied verbatim from the submodule
  for redistribution alongside the built DLL).

## Runtime version quirk (verified against source, not guessed)

`ZydisGetVersion()` returns the literal `ZYDIS_VERSION` macro
(`include/Zydis/Zydis.h`), which at commit `a2278f1d2` is hardcoded to
`0x0004000100000000` — major 4, minor 1, **patch 0**, build 0 — even though
the CMake project version (`CMakeLists.txt`, `project(Zydis VERSION 4.1.1.0 ...)`)
and the git tag both say `4.1.1`. The macro was not bumped for the 4.1.1 patch
release. `ZydisApi.pas`'s load-time version check must therefore compare
major/minor (`>= 4.1`), never expect an exact `4.1.1.0` match against
`ZydisGetVersion()` — an exact-match check would reject this exact DLL.

## Build environment

- Visual Studio 2026 Community, MSVC toolset `14.51.36231`
  (`cl.exe` reports `19.51.36248.0`).
- CMake: the copy bundled with Visual Studio,
  `Common7\IDE\CommonExtensions\Microsoft\CMake\CMake\bin\cmake.exe`.
- Generator: `NMake Makefiles` (avoids depending on Ninja being on `PATH`;
  both `cl` and `nmake` come from `VsDevCmd.bat`).
- Built: 2026-08-08. Relinked `/MT` on 2026-08-09 (increment 7, packaging —
  see "Runtime library: /MD vs /MT" below); same commit, same source, only the
  CRT linkage changed.

## Exact invocation

```bat
call "C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\Community\Common7\Tools\VsDevCmd.bat" -arch=x64 -host_arch=x64

cmake -G "NMake Makefiles" ^
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release ^
  -DCMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY=MultiThreaded ^
  -DZYDIS_BUILD_SHARED_LIB=ON ^
  -DZYDIS_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF ^
  -DZYDIS_BUILD_TOOLS=OFF ^
  -DZYDIS_BUILD_TESTS=OFF ^
  -DZYDIS_BUILD_MAN=OFF ^
  -DZYDIS_BUILD_DOXYGEN=OFF ^
  -DZYDIS_FEATURE_ENCODER=ON ^
  ..\zydis.submodule

cmake --build . --config Release
```

`ZYDIS_FEATURE_ENCODER=ON` is Zydis's default; it is listed explicitly because
the encoder is not currently used by `ZydisApi.pas` but costs nothing to keep
available for a later increment (e.g. NOP-filling a patched region).

`CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY=MultiThreaded` selects `/MT` (static, release CRT)
over CMake's default `MultiThreadedDLL` (`/MD`) — see "Runtime library: /MD vs
/MT" below for why.

This is exactly what `build_zydis.bat` in this folder runs (`cd /d %~dp0`,
resolve `VsDevCmd.bat` and `cmake.exe` by their absolute install paths, clean
`build\`, configure, build, copy `build\Zydis.dll` to `bin\x64\Zydis.dll`,
hash it). It is **not** called by `build_all.bat`, `scripts/build_dap.bat` or
`scripts/build_debug.bat` — those stay Delphi-only. Run it by hand, from the repo, any
time the pinned submodule commit changes:

```bat
git submodule update --init --recursive ThirdParty\Zydis\zydis.submodule
call ThirdParty\Zydis\build_zydis.bat
```

## Output

- `bin\x64\Zydis.dll` — 670,720 bytes (`/MT`; was 576,512 bytes as `/MD`, see
  below).
- SHA-256: `29a209ff95a2361e39a22e6d58aa16ada75e02d8c879363e5a9598ee9b93c34d`
  (also in `bin\x64\Zydis.dll.sha256`, regenerated by the build script via
  `certutil -hashfile ... SHA256`).
- One x64 DLL. The machine mode (32-bit vs 64-bit target code) is a decoder
  parameter passed at call time (`ZYDIS_MACHINE_MODE_LEGACY_32` /
  `ZYDIS_MACHINE_MODE_LONG_64`), not a build variant — verified by
  `DevTools\DisasmProbe.exe`, which decodes real bytes from both a 32-bit and
  a 64-bit `TestTarget.exe` through this one DLL.
- Exports verified with `dumpbin /exports` (43 total, unchanged by the /MT
  relink): `ZydisDisassembleIntel`, `ZydisGetVersion` and
  `ZydisIsFeatureEnabled` are present, matching what `ZydisApi.pas` imports.
- Runtime dependencies verified with `dumpbin /dependents`: `KERNEL32.dll`
  only. See below for the `/MD` numbers this replaced.

## Runtime library: /MD vs /MT (increment 7, packaging)

**Decided: `/MT` (static CRT).** The DLL is shipped to end users who may not
have the Visual C++ redistributable installed; `/MD` made the feature
correct-but-permanently-unavailable on such a machine (the CRT DLLs
`LoadLibrary` needs would simply not resolve). This is an optional single
dependency of an optional feature, so trading ~94 KB for removing an external
prerequisite is a clear win — a debugger that is otherwise a single
self-contained exe should not gain a hidden system-package dependency for one
optional DLL.

**Measured, both built from the identical pinned commit
(`a2278f1d254e492f6a6b39f6cb5d1f5d515659dc`), same CMake invocation except
`CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY`, on the build machine described above
(2026-08-09):**

| runtime | size (bytes) | `dumpbin /DEPENDENTS` |
|---|---|---|
| `/MD` (`MultiThreadedDLL`, CMake default) | 576,512 | `VCRUNTIME140.dll`, `api-ms-win-crt-runtime-l1-1-0.dll`, `api-ms-win-crt-string-l1-1-0.dll`, `KERNEL32.dll` |
| `/MT` (`MultiThreaded`, chosen) | 670,720 | `KERNEL32.dll` only |

Delta: +94,208 bytes (+16.3%). `dumpbin /EXPORTS` on the `/MT` build lists the
same 43 exports at different offsets — the CRT linkage change does not touch
the API surface. Functional parity confirmed, not just size/imports: rebuilt
every DevTools consumer (`DevTools\build_all.bat`) and re-ran
`DevTools\Win64\Debug\DisasmProbe.exe` against `TestTarget.exe`'s entry point
(RVA `$167FC0`) through the new `/MT` DLL — byte-identical decode to the
`/MD` build's known-good output from increment 1/2 (`push rbp` / `push rbx` /
`sub rsp, 0x98` / `mov rbp, rsp` / ... / `call 0x0000000000019F10` /
`call 0x0000000000166D00`).

`KERNEL32.dll` is always present on Windows, so `/MT` leaves the DLL with
effectively no external runtime dependency — a machine with nothing but a
stock Windows install can load it.

## Measured struct layout

`ZydisApi.pas` does not transcribe Zydis's structs. It reads a handful of
fields at byte offsets that were **measured** with a throwaway C program
compiled against the pinned headers, because `ZydisDecodedInstruction` is full
of nested unions and bitfields and one wrong field shifts every offset behind
it — silently: a wrong offset returns a plausible number from a neighbouring
field. `DebuggerTests\ZydisDetailTests.pas` pins every field below against
known encodings in both machine modes.

Measured 2026-11-27, commit `a2278f1d2`, `cl.exe` 19.51 x64 (the toolset the
DLL is built with). `ZYDIS_STATIC_BUILD` / `ZYCORE_STATIC_BUILD` only silence
the import declarations; nothing is linked.

| what | value |
|---|---|
| `sizeof(ZydisDisassembledInstruction)` | 1232 |
| `sizeof(ZydisDecodedInstruction)` | 328 |
| `sizeof(ZydisDecodedOperand)` | 80 |
| `sizeof(ZydisDecoder)` | 12 |
| `offsetof(ZydisDisassembledInstruction, info)` | 8 |
| `offsetof(ZydisDisassembledInstruction, operands)` | 336 |
| `offsetof(ZydisDisassembledInstruction, text)` | 1136 |

Fields of `ZydisDecodedInstruction`. The first column is the offset inside
`ZydisDisassembledInstruction` as the probe prints it; the second is relative
to the start of `info` (first column minus 8), which is what `ZydisApi.pas`
uses so that one table serves both the struct `ZydisDisassembleIntel` fills and
the one `ZydisDecoderDecodeInstruction` fills:

| field | in the disassembled struct | in `info` | type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `machine_mode` | 8 | 0 | 4-byte enum |
| `mnemonic` | 12 | 4 | 4-byte enum |
| `length` | 16 | 8 | `ZyanU8` |
| `encoding` | 20 | 12 | 4-byte enum |
| `opcode_map` | 24 | 16 | 4-byte enum |
| `opcode` | 28 | 20 | `ZyanU8` |
| `stack_width` | 29 | 21 | `ZyanU8` |
| `operand_width` | 30 | 22 | `ZyanU8`, bits |
| `address_width` | 31 | 23 | `ZyanU8`, bits |
| `operand_count` | 32 | 24 | `ZyanU8` |
| `operand_count_visible` | 33 | 25 | `ZyanU8` |
| `attributes` | 40 | 32 | `ZyanU64` |
| `meta.category` | 100 | 92 | 4-byte enum |
| `meta.branch_type` | 112 | 104 | 4-byte enum |
| `raw.prefix_count` | 120 | 112 | `ZyanU8` |
| `raw.modrm.mod` / `.reg` / `.rm` / `.offset` | 263 / 264 / 265 / 266 | 255 / 256 / 257 / 258 | `ZyanU8` each |
| `raw.sib.scale` / `.index` / `.base` / `.offset` | 267 / 268 / 269 / 270 | 259 / 260 / 261 / 262 | `ZyanU8` each |
| `raw.disp.value` | 272 | 264 | `ZyanI64` |
| `raw.disp.size` | 280 | 272 | `ZyanU8`, bits |
| `raw.disp.offset` | 281 | 273 | `ZyanU8` |
| `raw.imm[0].is_signed` | 288 | 280 | `ZyanBool` (1 byte) |
| `raw.imm[0].is_relative` | 289 | 281 | `ZyanBool` |
| `raw.imm[0].value` | 296 | 288 | `ZyanU64` / `ZyanI64` |
| `raw.imm[0].size` | 304 | 296 | `ZyanU8`, bits |
| `raw.imm[0].offset` | 305 | 297 | `ZyanU8` |
| `raw.imm[1]` | 312 | 304 | `sizeof(raw.imm[0])` = 24 |

Constants read by the same program: `ZYDIS_ATTRIB_HAS_MODRM` = 1,
`ZYDIS_ATTRIB_HAS_SIB` = 2, `ZYDIS_ATTRIB_IS_RELATIVE` = 128;
`ZYDIS_OPCODE_MAP_DEFAULT` / `_0F` / `_0F38` / `_0F3A` = 0 / 1 / 2 / 3;
`ZYDIS_BRANCH_TYPE_NONE` / `_SHORT` / `_NEAR` / `_FAR` = 0 / 1 / 2 / 3;
`ZYDIS_STACK_WIDTH_16` / `_32` / `_64` = 0 / 1 / 2;
`ZYDIS_MAX_INSTRUCTION_LENGTH` = 15, `ZYDIS_MAX_OPERAND_COUNT` = 10.

Not every measured field is read: `mnemonic`, `meta.category` and
`meta.branch_type` are listed so that a later need does not start with a new
measurement, but `ZydisApi.pas` classifies an instruction from `opcode`,
`opcode_map` and `raw.modrm.reg`, which need no table of generated enum values.

**To measure again** (after repinning the submodule, or changing the toolset):
a C file that includes `<Zydis/Zydis.h>` and prints
`offsetof(ZydisDisassembledInstruction, <field>)` for each row above —

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <Zydis/Zydis.h>
#define OFS(expr) printf("%-44s %5u\n", #expr, (unsigned)offsetof(ZydisDisassembledInstruction, expr))
#define SZ(type)  printf("sizeof(%-36s) %5u\n", #type, (unsigned)sizeof(type))
int main(void) {
    SZ(ZydisDisassembledInstruction); SZ(ZydisDecodedInstruction); SZ(ZydisDecoder);
    OFS(info.length); OFS(info.opcode_map); OFS(info.opcode); OFS(info.attributes);
    OFS(info.raw.modrm.mod); OFS(info.raw.sib.scale); OFS(info.raw.disp.value);
    OFS(info.raw.disp.size); OFS(info.raw.disp.offset);
    OFS(info.raw.imm[0].is_signed); OFS(info.raw.imm[0].value);
    OFS(info.raw.imm[0].size); OFS(info.raw.imm[0].offset); OFS(info.raw.imm[1].value);
    OFS(operands); OFS(text);   /* ... one line per field of the table */
    return 0;
}
```

— compiled and run in a scratch directory, never in the repository:

```bat
call "C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\Community\Common7\Tools\VsDevCmd.bat" -arch=x64 -host_arch=x64
set ZY=<repo>\ThirdParty\Zydis\zydis.submodule
cl /nologo /DZYDIS_STATIC_BUILD /DZYCORE_STATIC_BUILD /I"%ZY%\include" /I"%ZY%\dependencies\zycore\include" /I"<repo>\ThirdParty\Zydis\build" /I"<repo>\ThirdParty\Zydis\build\zycore" offsets.c /Fe:offsets.exe
offsets.exe
```

The two `build` include directories hold the export-configuration headers CMake
generates (`ZydisExportConfig.h`, `ZycoreExportConfig.h`); they exist once
`build_zydis.bat` has run. Then update the constants in `ZydisApi.pas` and this
table together, and run `ZydisDetailTests`.

## The decode-only entry points

`ZydisApi.ZydisDecodeDetail` without text does not go through
`ZydisDisassembleIntel`, which decodes every operand and formats the
instruction's text on each call. It keeps one `ZydisDecoder` per machine mode,
set up once with `ZydisDecoderInit` (stack width 64 for `LONG_64`, 32 for the
32-bit modes, 16 for the 16-bit ones — the same mapping `ZydisDisassembleIntel`
applies internally), and calls `ZydisDecoderDecodeInstruction` with a null
context. Both are among the DLL's 43 exports. Measured on 21.5 million
instructions of a 620 MB image: about 80 ns per instruction.

They are optional: when either export is missing the unit falls back to
`ZydisDisassembleIntel` and returns the same facts.

## Verification questions answered (docs/DISASSEMBLY_PLAN.md, increment 1)

1. **Version and API shape** — `ZydisDisassembleIntel` exists exactly as the
   plan assumed (`include/Zydis/Disassembler.h`), confirmed by both source
   inspection and the exports table above. See the version-quirk note above
   for the one surprise (`ZydisGetVersion()` under-reports the patch digit).
2. **Maintained Pascal bindings** — `zyantific/zydis-pascal` exists and is
   listed as an official Zydis binding (MIT). It is a full header translation
   (static AND dynamic linkage, `TZydisDecoder`/`TZydisFormatter` classes, the
   whole API surface), last updated 2023-11-20 — it predates this pinned
   `v4.1.1` tag (2025-02-16) and was not re-verified against it. Using it would
   also contradict the plan's already-decided design (minimal explicit-import
   surface, dynamic `LoadLibrary` with an app-owned version gate, only the two
   entry points actually used). Not adopted; `ZydisApi.pas` is hand-written.
3. **One DLL, both machine modes** — confirmed by the CMake option
   `ZYDIS_BUILD_SHARED_LIB` (no per-architecture build knob in Zydis's own
   CMakeLists) and empirically by `DisasmProbe.exe` decoding both a 32-bit and
   a 64-bit target through the single built DLL.
